description: We are a motivated team of developers building an Earth-to-Space Matchmaking Engine for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Think of it as a geographic "recommendation engine" that uses open-source satellite data to identify locations on Earth that physically match proposed landing sites and permanent bases on the Moon and Mars.
summary: TerraTwin is a geospatial machine learning system developed to identify locations on Earth that share physical characteristics with selected regions of the Moon and Mars. It addresses the challenge of comparing planetary environments by integrating remote sensing datasets, harmonizing geographical information into a common spatial framework, and analyzing 16 physical features across 110,393 planetary grid cells. Using weighted Gower similarity and machine learning models such as Random Forest, LightGBM, and PyTorch MLP, the system predicts potential terrestrial analogues for lunar and Martian locations. It also provides an interactive 3D web application for exploring planetary locations and visualizing Earth analogue predictions. This project is important because studying similar environments on Earth can support planetary research, geological comparisons, rover testing, and future habitat-site studies without relying entirely on expensive extraterrestrial missions. TerraTwin aims to make planetary analogue identification more systematic, scalable and accessible to researchers, while supporting scientific investigation and future space exploration.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

TerraTwin is a geospatial machine learning system developed to identify locations on Earth that share similar physical and environmental characteristics with selected regions of the Moon and Mars. It integrates planetary remote sensing datasets, including geographical, geological, topographical and thermal information, from Earth, the Moon and Mars. The system harmonizes these datasets into a common spatial framework consisting of 110,393 grid cells, each represented by 16 physical features.

It uses weighted Gower similarity to measure the resemblance between planetary locations and Earth's land regions. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, LightGBM and PyTorch MLP, are used to identify and predict potential terrestrial analogues. The results can be explored through an interactive 3D web application where users can select planetary locations, enter coordinates and view ranked Earth analogue predictions.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Helps researchers identify Earth environments that resemble selected lunar and Martian regions.
  • Reduces dependence on expensive and difficult extraterrestrial field investigations for preliminary analogue research.
  • Supports geological, topographical and environmental comparisons across planetary bodies.
  • Provides a systematic and reproducible approach to planetary analogue identification.
  • Enables interactive exploration of planetary locations and their potential Earth counterparts.
  • Supports research related to rover testing, mission simulations and future habitat-site studies.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our aim is to bridge the gap between Earth-based research and planetary exploration. By identifying terrestrial environments with comparable physical characteristics, TerraTwin can help researchers conduct experiments, study geological formations and investigate environmental conditions on Earth before planning similar activities on the Moon or Mars.

We hope to make planetary analogue identification more accessible, scalable and data-driven, contributing to future space exploration research and the scientific understanding of extraterrestrial environments.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware and software were used?

Programming Language:

  • Python

Machine Learning and Data Science:

  • Scikit-learn
  • Random Forest Regressor
  • LightGBM
  • PyTorch
  • Pandas
  • NumPy

Geospatial Datasets:

  • GMTED2010
  • Global Lithological Map (GLiM)
  • Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) DEM
  • USGS SIM 2969
  • Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA MEGDR)
  • Thermal Emission Spectrometer (TES)
  • USGS SIM 3292

Web Development and Visualization:

  • Three.js for interactive 3D planetary visualization
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • REST API

Development and Testing:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Joblib for model storage
  • Pytest for software testing

The project is software-based and uses planetary remote sensing datasets and machine learning. No specialized hardware is documented in the project report.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

TerraTwin combines planetary science, geospatial analysis and artificial intelligence into a unified platform. Instead of relying entirely on manual comparisons or individual expert observations, it introduces a computational approach to identifying potential Earth analogues for locations on the Moon and Mars.

Its creative aspects include:

  • Comparing three planetary bodies using a common spatial representation.
  • Combining geological, terrain, thermal and surface characteristics.
  • Applying weighted similarity measurements alongside multiple machine learning architectures.
  • Using an interactive 3D interface to make complex planetary comparisons easier to explore.
  • Supporting coordinate-based predictions beyond the four primary case-study locations.

6. What factors did the team consider?

Our team considered several physical and environmental factors to make cross-planetary comparisons meaningful:

  • Geology: Rock types, lithological classifications and geological formations.
  • Terrain: Elevation, slope and surface ruggedness.
  • Thermal characteristics: Diurnal temperature variation and thermal inertia.
  • Albedo: The amount of sunlight reflected by a planetary surface.
  • Spatial characteristics: Geographic coordinates, spatial distribution and approximately 55 km grid spacing.
  • Data quality: Dataset resolution, normalization, missing values, measurement differences and consistency across planetary bodies.
  • Similarity weighting: The relative importance of different physical features when calculating analogue similarity.
  • Planetary differences: Differences in gravity, atmosphere, radiation, water availability, volatile distribution and geological history.
